newsitem.title: GERMANY: German press slam Waigel, call for resignation.
newsitem.headline: German press slam Waigel, call for resignation.

text.p: The German press called for Finance Minister Theo Waigel's resignation on Wednesday after he retreated from a controversial plan to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves to help Germany qualify for Europe's single currency.

Waigel, speaking after coalition deputies baulked at his unpopular move on gold, said he and the central bank president Hans Tietmeyer had reached "a good compromise" that would transfer windfall profits to Bonn only next year.

German business daily Handelsblatt said Waigel had lost support within his own Christian Social Union in Bavaria, as well as in its sister party, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, over his proposal to revalue Bundesbank assets.

In a commentary it said Waigel had caused substantial political damage and that foreign commentators had "poured mockery and ridicule onto the German finance minister, the Bonn government coalition and the country as a whole".

"The irony is it was all in vain. Waigel did not get one step closer to fulfilling his aim to fulfil the Maastricht criteria." it said. "There is no way round it. The only thing left for Waigel is to resign."

The Frankfurter Rundschau daily said in a commentary the Bonn's gold crisis showed that Waigel was prepared to do anything just to cling on to his job and that the whole affair had made the coalition as fragile as a "house of cards".
"Many witnesses perceive the finance minister as one of those who exploit more tactics and tricks in office than normal simply to remain in power," the Rundschau said.

Mass-circulation daily Bild carried a report on its front page entitled: "Waigel's most difficult hour. Vote of confidence today" referring to a motion put forward by opposition Social Democrats and Greens calling for his resignation.
In a commentary Bild said that the Bonn coalition needed to inspire public confidence in the euro for it to succeed.
"(Public) confidence is not gained by permanent crisis meetings or party political cock-fighting," it said.
